089/**
090 * SSFormattedTextField extends the JFormattedTextField.
091 * This is the pivotal class for this package.
092 * It operates as a {@link SsComponent}.
093 * It locks focus while data is invalid and updates the database while editing.
094 *
095 * Note {@link #allValidate()} is used to do validation.
096 *
097 * The component can implement {@link #componentValidate() } to add additional
098 * checks (like date validation) beyond what is provided by the
099 * Formatter/FormatterFactory (which generally only handles display of values
100 * and/or character masks). Add application validity checks with
101 * {@link #setPluginValidator(dev.visdb.seesaw.decorators.Validator)}.
102 * <br>see {@link FormattedTextFieldVerifier} which locks focus while data is invalid.
103 * <br>see {@link SSFormattedTextFieldListener} which may update the database.
104 *
105 * @see <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.desktop/javax/swing/JFormattedTextField.html">JFormattedTextField</a>
106 */
107
108@SuppressWarnings("serial")
109public class SsFormattedTextField extends JFormattedTextField implements SsComponent {
110  /**
111   * This InputVerifier locks the focus down while the
112   * JFormattedTextField has invalid data.If non empty text do stringToValue
113   * validation check, then use {@link #allValidate()} for more validation checks.
114   * If the data is valid and the value is null then do
115   * "setValue(null)" to make sure the null formatter is used subsequently.
116   * <p>
117   * If weird errors occur, return true to avoid a focus lock hang.
118   */
119  public class FormattedTextFieldVerifier extends InputVerifier {
120    /**
121     * Check component text valid; allow focus change if it is.
122     * If weird errors are encountered, allow focus to change
123     * so focus doesn't get stuck.
124     * @param input Component to be validated/verified
125     * @return true if the input is valid, otherwise false
126     */
127    @Override
128    public boolean verify(JComponent input) {
129      // assert input == SsFormattedTextField.this;
130      final SsFormattedTextField ftf = (SsFormattedTextField) input;
131      Object value = null;
132      String formattedText = ftf.getText();
133      AbstractFormatter formatter = ftf.getFormatter();
134
135      logger.log((formatter == null || formattedText == null) ? Level.ERROR : DEBUG,
136                 () -> sf("FormattedText %s, Formatter %s", getColumnForLog(),
137                          formatter == null ? null : formatter.getClass().getSimpleName()));
138      if (formatter == null || formattedText == null)
139        return true; // Impossible. Just get out and let focus change.
140
141      boolean ok = true;
142      // Suppress "value" property change event if a call is made to setValue()
143      verifyingText = true;
144      try {
145        if (formattedText.isBlank())
146          logger.log(DEBUG, "formattedText is blank");
147        try {
148          // Convert the text looking for ParseError. Not like commitEdit().
149          value = formatter.stringToValue(formattedText);
150        } catch (ParseException pe) {
151          // Generally bad user input.
152          String finalFormattedText = formattedText;
153          logger.log(DEBUG, () -> sf("%s: '%s' Parse Exception offset %s.", getColumnForLog(),
154                                     finalFormattedText, pe.getErrorOffset()));
155          ok = false;
156        }
157
158        // Perform component and custom validation.
159        if (ok)
160          ok = allValidate().all();
161        // If ok with null, make sure to use the null formatter. Needed?
162        if (ok && value == null)
163          ftf.setValue(null); // Note: "verifyingText" skips pce.
164        // Update text decoration, e.g. red for negative.
165        if (ok)
166          decorateText();
167      } catch (final Exception e) {
168        // TODO: Not right. What runtime exceptions should be looked for?
169        logger.log(Level.ERROR, () -> getColumnForLog() + ": PROGRAM/RUNTIME ERROR");
170        ok = false;
171      } finally {
172        // Stop supressing "value" property change event handling.
173        verifyingText = false;
174      }
175      decorate();
176      return ok;
177    }
178  }
179
180  /**
181   * SSComponentListener for comp's "things have changed" event handler.
182   * Only handles "value" property.
183   */
184  protected class SSFormattedTextFieldListener implements PropertyChangeListener {
185    /**
186     * @param pce property change event
187     */
188    @Override
189    public void propertyChange(PropertyChangeEvent pce) {
190      if (pce.getPropertyName().equals("value"))
191        handleValuePropertyChange(pce);
192    }
193  }
194
195  /**
196   * Handle a "value" property change event; used to propagate changes back to
197   * bound database column.Avoid cascading events and always decorate. Does
198   * nothing if {@link #allValidate()} via decorate indicates invalid.
199   * @param pce "value" from property change event
200   */
201  private void handleValuePropertyChange(PropertyChangeEvent pce) {
202    final SsFormattedTextField ftf = this;
203
204    // OUCH: very weird, if either oldValue or newValue is null
205    //       then "value" property fires even when both are null.
206
207    // Ignore event if triggered by FormattedTextFieldVerifier.
208    if (verifyingText)
209      return;
210
211    // TODO: listener's bombarded when getting focus and null involved.
212    //       Use a document listener for doing "checkRowOK()";
213    //       then can avoid the Objects.equals stuff.
214    if (!checkRowOK(() -> {
215          // This short circuit for debugging.
216          //if (pce.getOldValue() == null && pce.getNewValue() == null)
217          //        return false;
218
219          try {
220            // This avoids extra dialogs.
221            JDBCType jdbcType = getColumnJDBCType();
222            Object v1 = convertToType(pce.getOldValue(), jdbcType);
223            Object v2 = convertToType(pce.getNewValue(), jdbcType);
224            // Avoid dialog if old and new are equal
225            return !Objects.equals(v1, v2);
226          } catch (SQLException ex) {
227            return true; // Dialog's OK
228          }
229        })) {
230      return;
231    }
232
233    final Object currentValue = ftf.getValue();
234
235    logger.log(DEBUG,
236               () -> sf("%s: to database '%s' type %s.", getColumnForLog(), currentValue,
237                        currentValue == null ? null : currentValue.getClass().getName()));
238
239    // TODO:  Should "postRowSetModifiedError be covered by dbChange()?
240
241    // The formatter says it's valid, but there's more to check
242    boolean someError = true; // set false after successfull database update
243    if (decorate()) {
244      try {
245        dbChange(() -> setColumnObject(currentValue));
246        someError = false;
247      } catch (SQLException ex) {
248        logger.log(Level.ERROR, (String) null, ex);
249      }
250    }
251    if (someError)
252      postColumnChangeStartError(ftf, currentValue);
253  }

314  /**
315   * Decorate after each text change.
316   * This is only so that the no arg constructor acts as expected.
317   * Any custom formatter is expected to decorate as needed.
318   */
319  private static class DecoratingFormatter extends DefaultFormatter {
320    private SsFormattedTextField ftf;
321
322    @Override
323    public void install(JFormattedTextField ftf) {
324      super.install(ftf);
325      this.ftf = ftf instanceof SsFormattedTextField comp ? comp : null;
326    }
327
328    @Override
329    protected DocumentFilter getDocumentFilter() {
330      return new DocumentFilter() {
331        @Override
332        public void replace(DocumentFilter.FilterBypass fb, int offset, int length, String text,
333                            AttributeSet attrs) throws BadLocationException {
334          super.replace(fb, offset, length, text, attrs);
335          modified();
336        }
337
338        @Override
339        public void insertString(DocumentFilter.FilterBypass fb, int offset, String string,
340                                 AttributeSet attr) throws BadLocationException {
341          super.insertString(fb, offset, string, attr);
342          modified();
343        }
344
345        @Override
346        public void remove(DocumentFilter.FilterBypass fb, int offset, int length)
347            throws BadLocationException {
348          super.remove(fb, offset, length);
349          modified();
350        }
351
352        private void modified() {
353          if (ftf == null)
354            return;
355          Utils.postColumnChangeStart(ftf, ftf.getText());
356        }
357      };
358    }
359  }

373  // TODO: plugin for default mono font and/or if should be used.

375  private void adjustFont() {
376    if (getFormatterFactory() instanceof MaskFormatterFactory) {
377      Font currentFont = getFont();
378      Font monoFont = new Font(Font.MONOSPACED, currentFont.getStyle(), currentFont.getSize());
379      setFont(monoFont);

383  /**
384   * Add custom focus behavior: gain selectAll, lose COMMIT_OR_REVERT.
385   * Related behavior.
386   */
387  @Override
388  public void customInit() {
389    // COMMIT_OR_REVERT SHOULD ALREADY BE THE DEFAULT
390    setFocusLostBehavior(JFormattedTextField.COMMIT_OR_REVERT);
391
392    // Adding focus listener to assist with highlighting and text selection
393    // addFocusListener(this);
394    addFocusListener(new FocusAdapter() {
395      @Override
396      public void focusGained(FocusEvent fe) {
397        // While focused, editing, show regular
398        // This assumes that decorate() is not invoked while this has
399        // focus, a JFormatterTextField characteristic.
400        if (getTextDecorator() instanceof NegativeNumberTextDecorator)
401          TextStyles.applyStyle((JComponent) SsFormattedTextField.this, TextStyles.RESET);
402        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> { selectAll(); });
403      }
404    });
405
406    // Setting inputVerifier to lock focus until valid.
407    setInputVerifier(new FormattedTextFieldVerifier());
408
409    addPropertyChangeListener("editValid", (e) -> {
410      logger.log(TRACE, sf("editValid: isValid %s", e.getNewValue()));
411      decorate();
412    });
413  }

452          removePropertyChangeListener("value", ((PropertyChangeListener) eventListener));
453        }

458  /**
459   * {@inheritDoc }
460   * <p>
461   * Only numeric, boolean and date types are handled.
462   *
463   * @see <a href="https://download.oracle.com/otn-pub/jcp/jdbc-4_3-mrel3-eval-spec/jdbc4.3-fr-spec.pdf">JDBC 4.3 Specification</a> Appendix B.3 JDBC Types Mapped to Java Object Types
464   */
465  private void updateJComponent() {
466    // TODO: put discussion of type handling/mapping elsewhere,
467    //       and reference it from here.
468
469    // It is OK to pass a String to SsFormattedTextField or a child class expecting a string (e.g., SSCuitField), but for
470    // child classes expecting a number format (e.g., SSCurrencyField) then it will not accept a string an an exception will be thrown.
471    //
472    // Previously, data type conversions for the component and rowset were handled with DbToFm() and updateRowSet().
473
474    // TODO Review date/time handling: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21162753/jdbc-resultset-i-need-a-getdatetime-but-there-is-only-getdate-and-gettimestamp
475
476    // SQL TO JAVA CONVERSIONS: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5251140/map-database-type-to-concrete-java-class
477    //
478    // 2020-09-14: Will use java <-> SQL mapping in JDBC to get appropriate Java object and then exclude ones that would cause a problem for JFormattedTextField
479    // Based on: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/sql/ResultSet.html#getObject-java.lang.String-
480    //
481    // getObject() will return the given column as a Java object. JDBC specification should contain the mappings for built in types.
482
483    try {
484      do {
485        // If no records, no columns, bail.
486        // TODO: is this check needed?
487
488        if (!getRowsModel().onActiveRow() || RowSetOps.getColumnCount(getRowSet()) == 0) {
489          // TODO: should this check allow null?
490          setValue(null);
491          break;
492        }
493
494        final Object dbValue = getColumnObject();
495
496        // If record field null then set value null, bail.
497        if (dbValue == null) {
498          // TODO: should this check allow null?
499          setValue(null);
500          break;
501        }
502
503        final JDBCType jdbcType = getColumnJDBCType();
504        if (!(checkConvertToJdbcType(jdbcType, dbValue.getClass(), null)))
505          logger.log(Level.ERROR,
506                     () -> sf("%s CAN'T CONVERT %s to %s", getColumnForLog(), jdbcType,
507                              dbValue.getClass().getName()));
508
509        // NOTE: H2's "rx.updateObject(idx, obj)" converts Date
510        //       to sql.Timestamp which is converted on commit (I guess)
511        //       to sql.Date
512        // Avoid need for "(newValue instanceof Date) ||".
513        // See RowSetOps.updateColumnObject().
514        final Object newValue = Boolean.TRUE ? convertToType(dbValue, jdbcType) : dbValue;
515
516        // Only support some Java types for JFormattedTextFields.
517        // TODO: Wonder if "newValue instanceof Number" would work.
518        // TODO: What if an installed formatter doesn't handle the type?
519        //       Where is that checked.
520        if ((newValue instanceof String) || (newValue instanceof Boolean)
521            || (newValue instanceof Float) || (newValue instanceof Double)
522            || (newValue instanceof Integer) || (newValue instanceof Long)
523            || (newValue instanceof java.math.BigDecimal) || (newValue instanceof java.sql.Date)
524            || (newValue instanceof java.sql.Time) || (newValue instanceof java.sql.Timestamp)) {
525          Object finalNewValue = newValue;
526          logger.log(DEBUG, () -> sf("%s: getObject() - %s", getColumnForLog(), finalNewValue));
527          setValue(newValue);
528        } else {
529          logger.log(Level.ERROR,
530                     sf("%s: JDBCType %s to %s not supported", getColumnForLog(), jdbcType,
531                        newValue != null ? newValue.getClass().getName() : null));
532          //
533          // TODO: there is no "setValue()". Should do "setValue(null)"?
534          //
535        }
536      } while (false);
537    } catch (SQLException sqe) {
538      logger.log(Level.ERROR, sf("%s: Exception updating rowset.", getColumnForLog(), sqe));
539      setValue(null);
540    }
541    decorateText(); // For example: color red for negative number
542    decorate();
543  }

545  /**
546   * Decorate text based on current value of this component.
547   * The following default text decorator distinguishes negative
548   * numbers. Typically red for negative numbers, otherwise black.
549   * Non numeric values are ignored.
550   * Override this method to do other things.
551   */
552  // Note: this might make more sense in NumberField.
553  // TODO: should this be updated while focused and any value change?
554  // TODO: should this be in SSComponentInterface?
555
556  static class NegativeNumberTextDecorator extends BaseTextDecorator {
557    @Override
558    public void decorateText() {
559      if (!(getSsComponent() instanceof SsFormattedTextField ftf))
560        return;
561
562      // TODO: if SsFormattedTextField not focus locked,
563      //       something special needed?
564
565      Object value = ftf.getValue();
566      boolean isNeg = switch (value) {
567        case Double val -> val < 0.0;
568        case Float val -> val < 0.0;
569        case Long val -> val < 0;
570        case Integer val -> val < 0;
571        case BigDecimal val -> val.signum() < 0;
572        case null, default -> false;
573      };
574      TextStyles.applyStyle(decoComp(),
575                            isNeg ? TextStyles.getStyle("negative_number") : TextStyles.RESET);
576    }
577  }
578

586    getDecorator().setDecorateTextEnabled(false);

596  /**
597   * Determine if there are user input characters. A formatted text field might
598   * contain only the format pattern and no input characters. If there is
599   * insufficient information to determine the result, true is returned.
600   * @return true if there is user input
601   */
602  @SuppressWarnings("UseOfSystemOutOrSystemErr")
603  public boolean containsUserText() {
604    AbstractFormatter f = getFormatter();
605    return switch (f) {
606      case MaskFormatter mf -> FormatterAssist.containsUserText(getText(), mf);
607      default -> {
608        if (f instanceof FormatterAssist fa) {
609          System.err.printf("**************\nNOTICE ME HERE: %s\n**************\n", fa);
610        }
611        yield !getText().isEmpty(); // TODO: isBlank()?
612      }
613    };
614  }
